answer: Each identity registers one orchard plot, locking a 60-credit bond. The plot publishes one harvest signal, with a fresh sample hashed on arrival. Depletion raises price: the k-th fake pays 60 plus 40+3(k-1), the 1,000th sample costs 3,037, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,598,500 total. An honest operator pays 100 once and recovers the 60 bond after a clean epoch. Auditors follow the thread from plot to signal to sample: a listed hash or claimed plot is rejected, and checked samples are destroyed. A sample-rental ring fails: rented samples already appear in the ledger, and reuse burns the bond.
